title: Agence Sénégalaise d’Études Spatiales — agency mandate
locator: PDF p. 36, ASES back-cover notice citing decree 2023-754
conditions: Senegalese agency notice published in the national press agency magazine in 2024.
supports: Establishes ASES’s policy, research and training mandate. It identifies the institution represented in the partner roster.
limits: No rover hardware, cabin specification or fire experiment is described.

title: SENSAT — GAINDESAT-1A
locator: Fiche technique and Comment ça fonctionne, including Balises au sol, Collecte en orbite and Transmission
conditions: Senegal’s SENSAT programme describes an Earth-orbiting CubeSat launched on 16 August 2024 to collect and relay environmental data from ground stations.
supports: Documents national experience with telemetry and orbital data collection. The source is a SENSAT programme record.
limits: Orbital satellite data cannot establish a planetary rover’s mass, wheels, atmosphere or fire response. No applicable public ASES rover specification was identified in the reviewed sources.

title: Agencia Espacial Española — Relaciones internacionales y bilaterales
locator: Programas bilaterales, paragraph headed Colaboración con la NASA
conditions: AEE attributes the HGAS antennas and the MEDA and REMS weather instruments on NASA’s Perseverance and Curiosity to Spain.
supports: Establishes Spain’s contribution to flown Mars rovers. CAB (CSIC–INTA) led MEDA as detailed in aee-02.
limits: The agency record attributes a national contribution. It supplies no complete rover or fire-system design.

title: CAB (CSIC–INTA) — MEDA envía el primer informe meteorológico desde el cráter Jezero en Marte
locator: PDF pp. 1–3, instrument description, first reading, and sols 43–44

quantities.quantity: Approximate measured wind gust for sols 43–44

conditions: The CAB-led suite flew on NASA’s Perseverance. Weather observations cover Jezero crater on 3–4 April 2021, ahead of the Ingenuity flight.
supports: Constrains an exposed Mars environmental sensor payload and provides an example of time- and site-specific weather data.
limits: The reported weather is local and outside the rover. A cabin temperature, ventilation rate, fire threshold or qualification range cannot be inferred.

title: Türkiye Uzay Ajansı — 2025 Performans Programı
locator: Printed p. 16 (PDF p. 20), performance indicator 2 for the lunar soft-landing project, explanatory paragraph
conditions: TUA describes the AYAP-2 soft-landing phase and preliminary work, including student teams, on a planned mobile rover.
supports: Establishes a planned lunar surface mobility activity in the second phase and the maturity of the public evidence.
limits: Programme completion percentages are administrative indicators. The document gives no measured rover mass, payload, speed or cabin values.

title: Türkiye Uzay Ajansı — Türkiye’nin Ay Yolculuğunda Geri Sayım Başladı
locator: 16 September 2026 announcement, paragraphs on integration, environmental testing and lunar orbit
conditions: The first Turkish deep-space spacecraft had completed assembly and integration and entered the system-level environmental test phase.
supports: Separates current phase-one spacecraft testing from the second-phase rover proposal in tua-01.
limits: The orbital spacecraft’s test programme and mass supply no ground mobility or cabin fire data for a rover.

title: Turkish Space Agency — AYAP-1
locator: Projects → Ongoing Projects → AYAP-1, programme objective
conditions: TUA frames lunar surface mobility as an objective of the overall Lunar Research Programme.
supports: Provides an English-language agency pointer to the programme. The detailed performance plan identifies the rover with its second phase.
limits: The page title alone does not establish phase-one rover hardware or surface operations.

title: MBRSC team — The Rashid rover: to guide the way for the next generation lunar missions and solar system exploration
locator: EGU 2021, first PDF page, rover specifications table, Mobility row
conditions: MBRSC’s mission engineers presented the Rashid-1 preflight design in 2021. The differential drive was intended to operate during lunar daylight.
supports: Supplies engineering targets for comparison with a small, uncrewed, exposed rover.
limits: This preflight configuration differs from the later dimensional summary in mbrsc-02. No successful surface operation confirmed these design targets.

title: Protocol Department of Dubai — Rashid 1 landing outcome and Rashid 2 announcement
locator: 26 April 2023, paragraphs on HAKUTO-R, the first Emirates Lunar Mission and the dimensions of the first rover
conditions: MBRSC built the first Rashid rover. Its HAKUTO-R carrier reached lunar orbit and the landing attempt on 25 April 2023 failed.
supports: Provides a government summary of approximate flight-vehicle dimensions and mission outcome.
limits: The dimensions refer to Rashid 1. Its lunar wheel performance, internal temperatures and survival time were never measured on the surface.

title: Hurrell et al. — Traction Performance Evaluation for a Rashid-1 Rover Wheel
locator: PDF pp. 4–6, §2.1 Single-Wheel Experiment, figures 1–3; §§3–4 for experiment versus simulation
conditions: The authors measured traction, sinkage and tracks using a rigid test wheel on a terrestrial rig, with loosely packed simulant at about 25% relative density. The flight wheel had an open structure and shorter grousers.
supports: Provides a component-level test method with declared loads, wheel geometry and slip conditions suitable for planning a validation experiment.
limits: Predicted performance at lunar gravity came from simulation. The ground wheel differed from flight hardware. These results supply no cabin fire data.

title: Firefly Aerospace — Blue Ghost Mission 2 manifest
locator: Mission Summary and Rashid Rover 2 payload section
conditions: Firefly lists MBRSC’s Rashid Rover 2 on an upcoming lunar far-side delivery targeted no earlier than 2027 in the manifest reviewed in November 2026.
supports: Identifies a planned wheel-material exposure experiment on the Moon’s far side.
limits: The announced test objective provides no measured durability or abrasion result.

title: Korea AeroSpace Administration — 원격 제어를 넘어 ‘자율 주행’을 위한 우주탐사 모빌리티에 AI 도입 추진
locator: 24 June 2026 press release no. 427, second and third body paragraphs, including ‘달의 낮 기간(14일 이내)’

quantities.quantity: Upper bound on the described lunar daytime operating period

conditions: KASA described its planned 2032 landing mission at an expert meeting on autonomous navigation and payload support.
supports: Documents a daylight mission concept and trade-offs between route energy and hazard avoidance.
limits: The quoted interval is a planning window. It supplies no measured battery endurance, night survival or flight-qualified specification.

title: Wang, Kim and Han — Experimental Analysis of Lunar Rover Wheel’s Mobility Performance Depending on Soil Condition and Wheel Configuration

quantities.quantity: Grouser height in the cross-soil comparison

conditions: The KICT researchers used a single-wheel terrestrial rig with KLS-1 Korean lunar simulant and Jumunjin sand. They compared drawbar pull, torque and sinkage under controlled slip.
supports: Provides an engineering test matrix showing that the same wheel responds differently to soil and grouser geometry.
limits: Research published in 2017 predates KASA. It is not a KASA-run test or a measurement of the planned national flight rover.

title: UK Space Agency — Mission to explore life on Mars one step closer as UK team to replace Russian components for Mars Rover
locator: 23 November 2023, paragraphs on Airbus Stevenage, Enfys and the drill sampling depth

quantities.quantity: Approximate intended maximum subsurface sampling depth

conditions: Airbus built Rosalind Franklin in Stevenage for ESA’s mission. UKSA funded the Aberystwyth-led Enfys instrument to select sampling targets. The drill depth is an overall rover system capability.
supports: Supports a sampling-tool reach requirement and documents the roles of UKSA, Airbus and the instrument team.
limits: The depth is a design capability. The source does not report a drilling operation on Mars or attribute construction of the drill to the UK team.

title: UK Space Agency — Airbus Defence and Space opens state-of-the-art Mars Yard
locator: 27 March 2014 announcement, paragraph containing Colin Paynter’s statement on the enlarged facility

quantities.quantity: Specially selected sand in the test arena

conditions: UKSA describes the Airbus ground-test facility in Stevenage where the ExoMars team could evaluate autonomous navigation in an enclosed analogue.
supports: Offers a dimensional reference for a terrain and navigation test course.
limits: The ground facility dimensions do not give a rover’s maximum climb angle or performance on Mars. Mission dates forecast in this historical announcement are obsolete.
